steps.content: The lights come on, so harsh that your eyes, though long used to bright light, narrow slightly. The Sinner in front of you, however, stares unblinkingly at you, as if her hostility toward you is strong enough to override her physiological instincts.
You don't like me, do you? Or should I say... hate me?
But I don't recall ever provoking or hurting you.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: You must've persecuted quite a few Sinners, by the sound of it.
Oh? Looks like someone told you that I'm a supervillain who persecutes Sinners.
Was this the same person who sent you to assassinate me?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: No one told me anything, and I don't need to be told to know how dangerous those darn shackles of yours are to us Sinners. Even a half-wit knows that.
She sneers and gives a shake of her hand, seemingly remembering the red thorns that appeared when the shackles pierced her body.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: You restrain Sinners with your shackles, lock them up in this place. I've seen it with my own eyes. I want to kill you, and that's my own decision!
She's stubborn. It seems you won't be able to get the information you need out of her by persuasion. You have to try a different approach.
test
test
test
test
test
test
I understand why you feel this way, but I can't just let this matter drop without giving it a try. Sorry.
Since you're not forthcoming... well, let me show you the information I've found about you. For instance, your residential records.
You used to report incidents to the authorities quite often, and as a result, there is no lack of biological information about you on record, so it wasn't difficult to find a match.
Thistle stares at you with cold eyes, as if waiting for you to make your move. You sigh and continue.
It's not my intention to reopen old wounds... You come from an FAC family, right?
And you tried very hard to seek revenge on behalf of your parents.
The girl in front of you remains silent, but you observe a slight tremble in her eyelids. So you open the file and start reading aloud.
Hills, female, father a member of the FAC, mother a homemaker. After her father died in battle in N.F. 103, she was raised by her mother alone, and they later moved to the outskirts of Eastside.
In N.F. 111, Hills reported her mother's disappearance to the Eastside Public Security Bureau, but no file was opened. Her mother never reappeared, which effectively made her an orphan.
Perhaps because she has her guard up, upon hearing these details of her past, there is only a brief moment of surprise before she quickly regains her composure.

These few lines of text encapsulate the hardships that Hills has endured, hardships that should be too overwhelming for a young girl to overcome. And yet it appears that she has turned the page and has been toughened by her circumstances.
Would someone go out of their way to kill you just because they picture you as a bad person and think you may harm them?
Perhaps this is the root of your hatred toward us, the powers that be? Because the Eastside Public Security Bureau did not fulfill its duties?

But this matter has nothing whatsoever to do with the MBCC Sinners, nor with the Bureau or me. Or did you encounter something else that inspired your hatred of us, like the incident that turned you into a Sinner?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Something else?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: I hate you because you're bullies who oppress the common people and bootlickers who do the bidding of the rich degenerates. That's reason enough!
It seems you're not going to tell me the truth. Well, it's understandable that you don't trust us. After all, you had no one to count on but yourself in your search for your mother.
The record shows that immediately after being refused help, you started looking for your mother on your own.

You were proactive. You did everything you could, and you did it by yourself. Asking passersby, putting up posters, letting the media know the injustice done to you and your mother... Very impressive, I must say.
But by the end of N.F. 111, you suddenly disappeared from the public eye, no longer active. No one knew where you went.
Why? Did someone approach you? Did this person offer to help you seek revenge and try to get you to join some organization?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: What if that was the case? What if it wasn't?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Is this what you've been trying so hard to pry out of me by playing the good guy?
She sees through your strategy, making it clear to you that she's not buying it.
The carrot approach is not working. A change of tactic is called for.
All right then, let's lay our cards on the table. Actually, it doesn't matter if you answer my questions or not, because I have already found a clue.
Not long ago, there was one other reckless assassin who came to the Bureau for me.
Your fighting styles were very similar. I guess you two are from the same organization. Her name is...
...Coquelic. Do you know her? Well, if you helped me wrap this up quickly, maybe I could take you to see her, before it's too late...
You draw out your words, trying to sound disdainful. It's far from an award-winning performance, but it successfully provokes the Sinner.
Despite all her efforts to conceal the raging fire of anger beneath her calm exterior, the shackles convey it to you, as well as her attempt to use her abilities to summon her Fire Blade.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: You're so obvious. Don't think I can't see through your little game. You're a lousy actor.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Continue with your performance, but you're never gonna get any information out of me.
Is that so? I may be an awful actor, but you're worse.
In case you don't already know, the shackles are an infallible lie detector.
She's speechless. This is the reaction you've been waiting for. Your strategy is working.

Truth be told, you wouldn't have resorted to such an extreme method, if it weren't for the fact that the clock is ticking for that person on the sickbed and you don't have the time to slowly coax the information out of Thistle.
From the look of things, you two really do belong to the same organization. It was she who brought you to the Garden in N.F. 111, wasn't it?
I hear they excel at exploiting character flaws, like anger and the desire for vengeance, by molding them into a force they can command.
This is probably what happened to you. You were deceived and manipulated, eventually becoming a knife in Coquelic's hands.
Did she promise you that, as long as you joined the Garden, you would have a chance to take revenge?
The president of the Future Foundation died at your hands. And that was the chance Coquelic promised you, the Garden's killer, wasn't it? You must be very grateful to her, right?
Thistle's expression looks nothing like that of someone whose darkest secret has just been exposed; she simply sneers.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Yes, I am a member of the Garden, and I am grateful to the Mentor. So what?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Yes, she created a chance for me to take revenge. She is always willing to take a chance on people like me, people in the gutter! Without her, we wouldn't have been able to survive, much less avenge ourselves.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: She is our Mentor, the best and strongest member of the Garden! Of course I'm grateful to her. You're not so delusional as to expect me to be grateful to you bastards, are you?
Thistle remains defiant and confrontational, making sharp retorts at every turn.
But you can tell from her clenched fists and her sudden talkativeness that she is reaching the limit of her patience.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Where were you when we were being persecuted? Where were you when we were being forced into a corner? Now that we've sorted things out ourselves, you're coming at us in the name of "justice"?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: You take us for pushovers? You think we won't fight back?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Well, let me tell you this: we're not something to be scoffed at!

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: That's why I'm targeting you. That's why I must get rid of you. And I will get rid of you. How about that, are you satisfied with this answer?
She's still hiding something. But this is the closest you've gotten to her true feelings. You know that one more step in the right direction, and you'll have a clear view of her inner self.
Get rid of me? That might be difficult for you. After all, even your "best and strongest" Mentor couldn't do it.

And that's the part I can't quite wrap my head around. I expected her, as your Mentor, to be much more cool-headed and cautious than you. So why would she attempt to assassinate me knowing full well that there was little chance of success?

At the very least, she should've brought some Garden members along, like you; that was just the smart thing to do from a professional standpoint. Given her physical condition at the time and the lack of help, her attempt on my life was doomed from the start.
Ah, I get it now. Is it because you're too weak, and she deemed you unworthy, so she didn't bring you along? She wanted nothing to do with you, did she?
After all, you couldn't even handle the Bureau's...
Clang!
Before you can finish your sentence, Thistle lunges at you; you've received no warning from the shackles.

Clearly, propelled by extreme fury, Thistle has experienced a burst of energy and has broken all the restrictions placed on her. She has crawled over the interrogation room's cold metal table, and is about to punch you straight in the face.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: Die! Die! Die!

As she has lunged at you, her body has hit the table, making a dull sound, but she doesn't cry out in pain, nor does she shrink back in the slightest, so intense is her fury and so determined is she to unleash that fury on your face.

She is opting for brute force over tactics or her special power. In this very moment, she is once again that helpless little girl from many years ago whose passion was the only thing that propelled her.
Looking into Thistle's eyes up close, you become more acutely aware of the intensity of her desire to kill you and of the foot of the desire.
Was Coquelic's reckless attempt on your life the product of the same logic?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Nightmare, protect the Chief!
In the nick of time, the door crashes open, and Nightmare swoops in, and lifting you by the back of your collar, swiftly transports you out of harm's way.
Nightingale and many others rush into the interrogation room, forming a protective semi-circle around you that separates you from the dangerous attacker.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief! Are you all right? Are you hurt? Do I have to remind you that you're still recovering?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: All right, get the A-Class Sinner under control first. Make sure she is completely incapacitated this time!

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The rest of you, get out of the way. Don't crowd around the Chief. Give the medical staff some space, so they can do their work.
Because of Nightingale's clear instructions, order is quickly restored in the interrogation room.
But Hecate pays no heed. She rushes to your side. Her voice trembles with fear when she speaks.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief, you... Didn't you say you knew you hadn't fully recovered and wouldn't provoke her?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: If... If Adjutant Nightingale hadn't been keeping a close watch on you, and if we hadn't arrived in time to protect you, what would have become of you?
All right, all right... I'm totally fine. You can see it for yourself. Don't be mad now. I promise I won't do it again...
You console the MBCC members gathered around you, listening to their complaints, making promises. Their voices somehow make the interrogation room feel like a home, even just for a while.
Still...

While receiving caring words and concerned looks, you've never taken your eyes off the young Sinner sitting on the floor for a moment. She keeps her head down. You can't see her expression, but you know she hasn't given up.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: <size=30>...Don't think this will dissuade me from my goal... It won't...</size>

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: <size=30>I may not be able to go after you now, or save the Mentor, but it won't stay this way forever...</size>
Thistle's voice is low but firm. She is feeling frustrated at yet another failure, but is trying hard to turn the frustration into a motivator.
You sigh and walk toward her.
You silly child, you can't hurt me. As you've seen, I'm surrounded by people who would do anything to protect me, much like you would do anything to protect your Mentor.
So I wouldn't say what you did was wrong. I believe that, the way you saw it, that was the best course of action open to you.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: ...What are you trying to say?
What I'm saying is, your escapade has given me a new perspective. Thanks to you, I now understand why that woman was so desperate to take my life.

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: What do you mean?
Her eyes widen. She looks deflated. The anger and resentment are gone. In their place is panic, an emotion you haven't seen her display until now.
She's scared that her recklessness might have become a blade that will be used to hurt her Mentor, and that unwittingly, she has once again helped someone pry into her Mentor's plans.
Now... Cough, cough...
Let someone you trust more explain it all to you. After her explanation, you might look at the situation from a whole new perspective.
You cough into your hand and then nod at Nightingale.
Nightingale leaves the room. A moment later, she returns, followed by a girl dressed in detective attire.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Look at the state of you! Why do you always look a mess every time I see you?

steps.speaker: Thistle
steps.content: It's you...?!

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: What, are you not pleased to see me? I heard an old acquaintance of mine was causing havoc again because of her impulsive tendencies, so I dropped everything and rushed back.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: You seem to have quite a few misunderstandings about the MBCC. I'll set you straight. But let's have those wounds looked at first. Come, follow me...
